African Communities Together and The Door brought the lawsuit last summer, after courthouse arrests tore apart families attending immigration appointments in New York City.

The stay followed a DOJ admission earlier this year that it had misinterpreted the policy memo used to justify courthouse arrests. Judge P. Kevin Castel halted the practice in May. The arrests continued within days.
Court records show at least one man's only criminal history was a trespassing charge from crossing the border. His attorneys argue the government cannot reasonably call him a threat to public safety.

An ICE supervisor defended the arrests in a sworn declaration, calling the courthouse the safest place to arrest people because at-large arrests in New York "tend to trigger protests and intervention by agitators and bystanders."

ICE arrested at least five immigrant New Yorkers at the 26 Federal Plaza courthouse after a federal judge halted the practice in May. The Justice Department is now fighting to conceal ICE's specific reasons for those arrests. 🧵
